change: Added a bounded immutable scalar backing index using one shared ownership-provenance traversal. The generic selected-allocation helper reuses that traversal. Window task partition/evaluation can reuse trusted indexed string/bigint charges while still detaching mutable containers. Parquet builds the index only when two source-sized extents no longer fit in available headroom; failed optional index admission cleans up and falls back to admitted copying.

edgeCases: partition/evaluation save more than 38000 reservation bytes for a 20000-character payload
source and index disposal do not invalidate retained output text
mutable byte mutation does not affect detached output
failed index admission keeps source charge intact
opaque external owners are not treated as proven atomic backing
real Parquet 64-row large-string task succeeds under 4 MiB with over 2 MiB retained output payload

measuredTradeoff.latency: Index construction adds CPU overhead in several local cases; copying remains the default when available headroom fits two source-sized extents.

limits: The headroom heuristic is a planning estimate; admission still rejects allocations that do not fit.
Index metadata is charged but reservation units are not portable VM heap measurements.
No broad end-to-end speedup is claimed.
Aggregate accumulator ownership, complete allocation matrix and production Worker memory acceptance remain open.
